answer: Each new identity must pass a random panel. Every tide draws five reviewers, and the applicant posts a 40-credit bond locked until the panel votes. The panel checks work and funding, and votes go on the public reef ledger, so a bribed vote stays visible. The k-th fake needs a fresh panel and 60 credits to bribe three of five, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 including bonds, with no reuse. An honest applicant pays one 40-credit bond, refunded on approval. A whisper ring selling votes fails because resampling breaks repeat panels, and a caught panelist loses a 100-credit stake.
